items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: I went to work with a fella by the name of Jack Pettis... So I went to work with him.

ctx.x: I made a bunch of them in New York. Now, I went to, when I, I went to work New York, I first went to work in a, a laundry. You know these Chinese, they used to call them laundries. Well I worked in the laundry for about six, seven months. And then I went to work with a fella by the name of Jack Pettis, who originally played with the Rhythm Kings. And then went with Ben Burnie. Well after he left Ben Burnie, he made up his own band. So I went to work with him. Perini was in the band. And this boy that committed…
You're all on a lot of mistakes. Yeah.

items.q: I played a lot of vaudzo myself with a fellow by the name of Jack Pettis

Yeah, he was 20 years ago. He sounded about as good on that thing, starting with some barbecue as you've ever heard him. Let's take this. Well, I was glad the minute I heard that, I figured it was that band because I was so familiar with that band. I played a lot of vaudzo myself with a fellow

by the name of Jack Pettis, and we used to run across Louis every once in a while, you know. Let's take one more break here, and then we'll come back and listen to some more from that album, and also some old Duke Ellington that's kind of interesting. We'll be back on jazz review after this word. Now, a few words about the Sony 250A tape deck. Forget it. Forget about leaving it on.
